transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-14
Start time: 09:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Diaz (Redwood); Nora Singh, Tomás Alvarez, Priya Menon, Elliot Reed (Cerulean)

Summary (auto):
Cerulean is evaluating Redwood for payment fraud scoring and customer support automation. Primary blockers: strict EU data residency, contractual subprocessor transparency, and a requirement to bring their own KMS for key management. Discussed geofencing options, region pinning policies, KMS integration patterns (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed), and next steps to exchange SOC2 docs and a sample subprocessor map.

Topics covered:
- How Redwood enforces region pinning and what "EU-only" means in practice
- Cross-border processing triggers (log forwarding, backups, metrics)
- Subprocessor list and where logs/metrics are stored
- KMS onboarding (customer-managed keys) and where encryption/decryption occurs
- Audit logs retention and exportability
- SSO / SAML scoping for RBAC and admin access

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript (selected snippets, timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, I'll kick us off — Marco's our solutions engineer — he's going to go deep on region controls and KMS. Nora, thanks for taking the time, maybe quick 30 second context from Cerulean?
[00:18] Nora Singh: Sure, yeah uh, Cerulean's security lead. We're re-evaluating vendors for any system that touches cardholder-adjacent data. Big thing for us is EU resident processing — we need, like, proof that PII and derived embeddings don't leave EU. Also subprocessor lock-down — we need a list and indemnities.
[00:35] Marco Diaz: Totally, makes sense. At a high level Redwood supports "region pinning" — you can pin a model route to a region, enforce compute location, and we have controls to avoid cross-region KV cache leaks. We'll show examples in a minute.
[00:49] Tomás Alvarez: Quick Q — what about logs? Metrics and audit logs, are those replicated globally for analytics? We can't have raw logs egress out of EU.
[01:04] Marco Diaz: Good question. By default our observability pipeline aggregates metrics in the region, but some telemetry (anonymized usage metrics) may be sent to a central control plane. For enterprise/private customers we can provide region-local telemetry and audit logs — typically retained in the customer's chosen region.
[01:26] Priya Menon: When you say "can provide" — I need to see it in the contract. Also need to know what subprocessor contracts look like and whether there's an ability to require EU-only subprocessors.
[01:40] Lena Park: Yep, we can share the subprocessor inventory; we also have contract language addenda for EU sovereignty. I'll include the standard addendum in the follow-up.
[01:53] Elliot Reed: Are backups included? It's important backups or cold storage don't go outside EU for certain datasets.
[02:05] Marco Diaz: Backups are configurable. For Hosted we default to region-local backups, but auxiliary backups or long-term archives may live in separate storage regions; with Redwood Dedicated or Private we can guarantee local-only backups. We'll send the precise backup policy doc.
[02:26] Nora Singh: KMS — we intend to BYOK (bring your own key) for everything that touches sensitive data. How does Redwood integrate with an external KMS — is encryption done client-side or server-side?
[02:43] Marco Diaz: Two patterns: customer-managed server-side keys (you provide a vault in the same region, Redwood calls the KMS for decrypt ops in-region), or client-side encryption where you encrypt payloads before sending. For your use-case, server-side BYOK with regional KMS is the common path — Redwood never persists plaintext outside the region. There are caveats — cold cache writes and some metadata may still touch the control plane.
[03:10] Tomás Alvarez: That caveat is the crux — what metadata are we talking about? System-level logs? Request IDs?
[03:22] Marco Diaz: Things like non-PII telemetry, model selection headers, billing counters. We can scoping redact or disable certain telemetry streams per customer contract. Full audit logs (request/response bodies) can be kept region-local and exported to your S3 in-region.
[03:40] Nora Singh: And what's the latency hit if we force everything into a single EU region vs allowing US fallback? Our fraud scoring is latency-sensitive.
[03:52] Marco Diaz: There's definitely impact. If you pin to eu-west-1 and Redwood routes all inference there, throughput and latency depend on fleet size and model sharding. We can provision Dedicated pools in EU to meet your SLOs — that reduces cross-border to zero but is more expensive. We'll provide a perf/cost estimate for eu-only Dedicated vs hosted with geo-fallback.
[04:18] Lena Park: For procurement, Priya, we'll add the SLA and the dedicated capacity pricing in the follow-up.
[04:28] Priya Menon: Sounds good. On subprocessors, can you clarify which parties have access to logs? For example, do any infra vendors (managed k8s, cloud provider) have access to PII or plaintext?
[04:43] Marco Diaz: Short answer: no plaintext access. Infrastructure vendors may have access to encrypted blob storage but not the keys. Our subprocessors are typically cloud providers and monitoring vendors; access to keys is restricted to the customer's KMS or our hardened HSMs under contract. We'll provide a redacted subprocessor matrix with access levels.
[05:05] Tomás Alvarez: Will there be an option to self-host the control plane? We want to avoid any central control-plane metadata leaving region borders.
[05:15] Marco Diaz: We offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where the control plane is customer-hosted; in those setups the control plane and logs never leave the environment. That is more involved but aligns with your sovereignty needs.
[05:29] Nora Singh: Ok, good. A few edge cases — what about model updates or fallback to smaller models in a different region if primary capacity is full? Does that trigger cross-border processing?
[05:44] Marco Diaz: By default routing policies are transparent — if you allow cross-region fallback, then yes it could. But you can define a policy: strict, no-fallback. With strict mode Redwood will queue requests or failover to a compatible model in-region (we also support auto-fallback to quantized variants in the same region).
[06:05] Priya Menon: Another legal question — retention windows for encrypted logs. Our compliance says logs must be kept for 7 years, but stored encrypted and accessible for audits. Can Redwood support long retention in-region?
[06:20] Marco Diaz: Yes — we can configure retention policies and export encrypted archives to your in-region S3 or object storage. Access control can be tied to your SSO and audit logs exported on-demand.
[06:35] Tomás Alvarez: SSO — we use SAML-based IdP and want RBAC that maps to our internal groups. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[06:48] Lena Park: Redwood supports SAML + SCIM provisioning, can map groups to roles, and tokenized admin actions. Marco, you want to add the details?
[06:56] Marco Diaz: Sure — you map IdP groups to roles (admin, dev, ops). We support just-in-time provisioning and SCIM sync for user lifecycle. Admin actions are logged in the audit trail and can be forwarded to Cerulean's log collector.
[07:12] Elliot Reed: Is the audit trail tamper-evident? We need to demonstrate chain-of-custody for logs during audits.
[07:22] Marco Diaz: We offer append-only log export and HMAC-signed log bundles for attestations. For Private deployments we can plug into your key management to sign logs.
[07:34] Nora Singh: Can you walk me through a hypothetical flow — payment event comes in, we send an inference request, what stays in EU? Walk us through request path.
[07:47] Marco Diaz: (walkthrough) Request hits our EU ingress, lives on EU compute, model KV cache stays in-GPU, request/response bodies are logged to in-region storage. If you use customer-managed KMS, the decryption calls happen inside the EU KMS; Redwood only sees ciphertext if you choose that. Control plane metadata — like routing decisions — may be accessible from the control plane; we can reduce that footprint or move the control plane in Private.
[08:20] Tomás Alvarez: Are there sample configs we can try? IaC module or terraform snippets?
[08:27] Marco Diaz: Yes, we'll share a terraform module for region pinning, sample policy yaml, and a small runbook for KMS onboarding.
[08:36] Nora Singh: Ok, question about subprocessors — any third-party vendors in US that could conceivably touch data? For example, do you use US-based logging processors?
[08:49] Lena Park: We do sometimes utilize global vendors but for enterprise we can arrange EU-only subprocessors or ensure the vendor processes EU data within region boundaries. We'll provide the list and the access levels.
[09:02] Priya Menon: Let's talk timeline — if we want to pilot in Q1, what do you recommend?
[09:10] Marco Diaz: Pilot with Redwood Hosted in eu-west-1 with strict region pinning but allow a small set of non-PII telemetry to flow to control plane for debugging. Alternatively, pilot with a Dedicated pool in EU — longer lead time, but easier to validate latency/SLOs. For KMS we can do an initial integration test, then a 2-week soak.
[09:34] Lena Park: Great. I'll send the SOC2 + standard addendum and Marco will push the terraform snippets and region pin policy. We should schedule a KMS deep-dive w/ Tomás and your infra team — how's the week of Dec 22?
[09:48] Tomás Alvarez: Works for us. I'll try to get the workload inventory by Dec 20.
[09:54] Nora Singh: Perfect. Anything else?
[09:57] Lena Park: That's it from us — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items discussed.

End of meeting.
